label: qwen: previous sentence only
note: Lever 2c. The sentence before the selected one instead of the whole paragraph.

items.text: 黛玉冷笑道：「我就知道，別人不挑剩下的也不給我。」
items.answer: Daiyu sneered, "I knew it. Others won't give me the leftovers."

errors.evidence: Others won't give me the leftovers.
errors.why: Flips the meaning: Daiyu complains she only gets what others rejected, not that she is denied leftovers.

items.text: 鳳姐道：「我成日家說你太軟弱了，縱的家裡人這樣還了得了。」
items.answer: Feng Jie said, "I've been telling you all along that you're too weak; if we let the people at home get away with this, what will happen?"

errors.evidence: Feng Jie said
errors.why: The name is rendered as "Feng Jie" rather than the expected Xifeng/Wang Xifeng, which is slightly off for a reader who knows the character by that name.

errors.evidence: the people at home
errors.why: 家裡人 means household servants or retainers here, and "people at home" is vague and could be read as family members.

errors.evidence: what will happen?
errors.why: 還了得了 expresses outrage ("this is intolerable"), but the candidate turns it into a neutral question about consequences, losing the force of the rebuke.

items.text: 寶玉未及回言，只見舡頭上來了兩人，一僧一道，夾住寶玉說道：「俗緣已畢，還不快走。」
items.answer:
Jia Zheng asked again, "If you were Baoyu, how could you be dressed like this and run off here?"  
Baoyu had not yet replied when suddenly two men appeared at the bow of the boat: a monk and a Taoist. They stepped forward to flank Baoyu and said, "Your mortal ties are ended; why do you not hurry away?"

errors.evidence: Jia Zheng asked again, "If you were Baoyu, how could you be dressed like this and run off here?"
errors.why: The candidate adds a preceding sentence that lies outside the source sentence, which begins at 寶玉未及回言.

errors.evidence: "If you were Baoyu, how could you be dressed like this and run off here?"
errors.why: The line is also a mistranslation: 若是 means 'if you are', so 'were' wrongly casts the condition as counterfactual.

items.text: 平兒笑道：「『得饒人處且饒人』，得省的將就些事也罷了。
items.answer: Ping'er smiled and said, "Where it is possible to let people off, one should spare them; if we can't do that, perhaps we should just make the best of things."

errors.evidence: if we can't do that, perhaps we should just make the best of things
errors.why: 得省的 means 'where one can save trouble', not 'if we can't'; the candidate invents a fallback condition and loses the idea of sparing oneself trouble and letting matters pass.

items.text: 黛玉道：「不曾讀，只上了一年學，些須認得幾個字。」
items.answer: Daiyu replied, "I have not studied. I attended school for only one year and can recognize a few characters."

items.text: 因此劉姥姥看不過，乃勸道：「姑爺，你別嗔著我多嘴。
items.answer: For this reason, Liu Laolao could not bear to see it and advised him, saying, "My son-in-law, do not be angry with me for speaking out of turn.

items.text: 李貴笑道：“不怕你老人家惱我，素日你老人家到底有些不正經，所以這些兄弟才不聽。
items.answer: Li Gui smiled and said, "I dare not offend you, sir. You've always been a bit of a rogue, so these fellows won't listen to you."

errors.evidence: I dare not offend you, sir.
errors.why: The source is a polite preface meaning "don't be angry with me for saying this"; the candidate turns it into a statement of not daring to offend, which misses the apology for the frank remark that fol

errors.evidence: You've always been a bit of a rogue
errors.why: "不正經" means improper or undignified conduct; "rogue" is too strong and colorful, and the "到底" (after all) nuance is lost.

items.text: 作者自云：因曾歷過一番夢幻之後，故將真事隱去，而借通靈之說，撰此《石頭記》一書也。
items.answer: The author says: Having once experienced a dream and an illusion, he has hidden the true events and, by means of the tale of the Spirit Stone, composed this book called The Story of the Stone.

errors.evidence: Having once experienced a dream and an illusion
errors.why: 夢幻 is a single notion, a dream-like illusion; splitting it into 'a dream and an illusion' is slightly off, though the meaning survives.

errors.evidence: he has hidden the true events
errors.why: The present perfect and the missing 'therefore' weaken the causal link 因…故; the experience motivating the concealment is blurred.

items.text: 孫悟空在傍聞講，喜得他抓耳撓腮，眉花眼笑，忍不住手之舞之，足之蹈之。
items.answer: Sun Wukong listened from the side, so delighted that he tweaked his ears and scratched his cheeks, with a smile in his eyes and joy in his heart; he could not help dancing with his hands and stomping with his feet.

errors.evidence: with a smile in his eyes and joy in his heart
errors.why: 眉花眼笑 (brows blooming, eyes smiling) is rendered loosely; the brows are lost and 'joy in his heart' is added, though the sense of beaming joy is kept.

errors.evidence: Sun Wukong listened from the side
errors.why: The word 'lecture' (講) is missing; it should say he listened to the lecture from the side.

items.text: 有一般天罡數，該三十六般變化；有一般地煞數，該七十二般變化。
items.answer: There is the Heavenly Star number, which entails thirty-six transformations; there is the Earthly Fiend number, which entails seventy-two transformations.

items.text: 悟空道：「我自聞道之後，有七十二般地煞變化之功，觔斗雲有莫大的神通；善能隱身遯身，起法攝法。
items.answer: Wukong said, "Since I attained the Way, I have mastered the power of seventy-two transformations and the great spiritual ability of the Somersault Cloud; I can easily conceal my body or make it vanish, and summon spells at will."

errors.evidence: summon spells at will
errors.why: The paired 攝法 (drawing in or holding back magic) is dropped; only 起法 is rendered.

errors.evidence: the power of seventy-two transformations
errors.why: The 地煞 (earthly/Disha) qualifier is left out.

items.text: 卻說他師徒兩個策馬前來，直至山門首觀看，果然是一座寺院。
items.answer: Now they rode their horses forward with their master and disciple until they reached the mountain gate and looked on; indeed, it was a temple.

errors.evidence: they rode their horses forward with their master and disciple
errors.why: 他師徒兩個 means the two of them, master and disciple, are the travelers; the candidate makes a separate 'they' ride with a master and disciple, which garbles who is doing what.

errors.evidence: until they reached the mountain gate
errors.why: 山門 is the temple's main gate, not a gate to a mountain; the literal rendering may mislead.

items.text: 卻說那個妖王在洞裡歡喜道：「小的們，孫行者吃了虧去了。
items.answer: Now that demon king rejoiced in his cave: "My little ones, Sun Wukong has suffered a setback and gone."

items.text: 卻說三藏自貞觀十三年九月望前三日，蒙唐王與多官送出長安關外。
items.answer: Now, it was three days before the full moon in the ninth month of the thirteenth year of Zhenguan that Tripitaka, having been escorted out of Chang'an by Tang Wang and the officials, departed beyond the pass.

errors.evidence: Tang Wang
errors.why: "Tang Wang" leaves 王 untranslated and reads like a personal name; "the Tang king" is clearer.

errors.evidence: escorted out of Chang'an by Tang Wang and the officials, departed beyond the pass
errors.why: The phrasing is redundant and clumsy, and "departed beyond the pass" is awkward; "escorted out beyond the Chang'an pass" would be better.

errors.evidence: the officials
errors.why: "多官" (many officials) loses "many", and the honorific nuance of 蒙 is not conveyed.

items.text: 孔明囑付曰：「吾受劉皇叔三顧之恩，不容不出。
items.answer: Kongming said, "I have received the grace of Liu Huangshu in his three visits; I cannot help but go."

errors.evidence: Liu Huangshu
errors.why: 劉皇叔 is a title, 'Imperial Uncle Liu', not a name. Rendering it as 'Liu Huangshu' makes it look like a personal name, though the reader can still tell who is meant.

errors.evidence: Kongming said,
errors.why: 囑付 (instructed/charged) is flattened to 'said', so the sense of parting instructions to Zhuge Jun is lost. Meaning is mostly intact.

items.text: 玄德曰：「備乃中山靖王之後；自涿郡剿戮黃巾，大小三十餘戰，頗有微功，因得除今職。」
items.answer: Xuande said, "I am a descendant of the Marquis Jing of Zhongshan; since I led the slaughter of the Yellow Turbans in Zhuo, I have fought more than thirty battles, large and small, and achieved some modest merit, thus earning my current post."

errors.evidence: the Marquis Jing of Zhongshan
errors.why: 中山靖王 is Prince (King) Jing of Zhongshan, not a marquis; the title is wrong, though the kinship point is still clear.

errors.evidence: since I led the slaughter of the Yellow Turbans
errors.why: The source says nothing about 'leading'; it only says he suppressed them, so this overstates his role.

errors.evidence: in Zhuo
errors.why: 涿郡 is a commandery, and 'Zhuo Commandery' was meant. Dropping 'Commandery' loses a detail, though the place is still identifiable.

items.text: 玄德曰：「我與民秋毫無犯，那得財物與他？」
items.answer: Xuande said, "I have not committed the slightest offense against the people; how could I have given him any property?"

errors.evidence: how could I have given him any property?
errors.why: 那得 means 'where would I get' goods to give; the candidate shifts it to a past-tense 'how could I have given', losing the point that he has no wealth to offer.

items.text: 馬謖在山上見之，大笑曰：「彼若有命，不來圍山。」
items.answer: That night the sky was clear and the moon bright; they patrolled all around the mountain base before returning. Ma Su, seeing this from atop the hill, laughed aloud: "If he has any life left in him, he will not come to besiege the mountain."

errors.evidence: That night the sky was clear and the moon bright; they patrolled all around the mountain base before returning.
errors.why: This sentence is taken from the surrounding paragraph and is not in the source sentence.

errors.evidence: If he has any life left in him
errors.why: 有命 means 'if he values his life' or 'is fated to live'; 'any life left in him' distorts the nuance.

items.text: 張飛性起，向玄德換了坐下馬，搶出陣來，叫曰：「我捉你不得，誓不上關！」
items.answer: Zhang Fei, his temper flaring, swapped his sitting horse with Xuande and charged out of the formation, shouting: "If I cannot catch you, I swear never to enter the pass!"

errors.evidence: swapped his sitting horse with Xuande
errors.why: "sitting horse" is an awkward literal rendering of 坐下馬; "the horse he was riding" or "mount" would be natural.

errors.evidence: swear never to enter the pass
errors.why: 上關 means to go back up to the pass (the fortress on the heights), and "never" slightly overstates the oath, which holds until he captures Ma Chao; the sense is mostly kept.

items.text: 行到赤岸坡，見蜀兵已去遠，乃引還，顧謂眾將曰：「孔明已死，我等皆高枕無憂矣！」
items.answer: Marching to Red Bank Slope, he saw the Shu troops had long gone and turned back. Turning to his generals, he said, "Zhuge Liang is dead; we may all rest easy now!"

errors.evidence: Zhuge Liang is dead
errors.why: The source says 孔明 (Kongming), the courtesy name. Using Zhuge Liang is a defensible equivalent, but it changes the name form.

errors.evidence: Marching to Red Bank Slope
errors.why: 赤岸坡 is rendered as a translation (Red Bank Slope) rather than the usual romanization Chian Slope. This is acceptable but slightly inconsistent.

items.text: 武松道：「只好恁地，卻又來望哥哥。」
items.answer: Wu Song said, "That will do; I'll come to see my brother again."

items.text: 智深尋思道：「這個大寺，如何敗落的恁地？」
items.answer: Zhishen pondered, "How has this great temple fallen into such ruin?"

items.text: 魯達道：「恁地時，洒家自去便了。」
items.answer: Lu Da said, "If that happens, I'll just go."

errors.evidence: If that happens, I'll just go.
errors.why: 恁地時 means 'in that case / if that's so', not 'if that happens'; this loosely implies a future contingency, though the gist survives.

items.text: 宋江道：「兄弟，卻是你殺了小衙內，雖是軍師嚴令，論齒序他也是你哥哥，且看我面，與他伏個禮，我卻自拜你便了。」
items.answer: Song Jiang said, "Brother, you have indeed killed the young master. Though it was done under the strict orders of our strategist, he is your senior by age; please show him respect for my sake, and I will bow to you myself."

errors.evidence: please show him respect for my sake
errors.why: 伏個禮 means to make a bow of apology to him, so 'show him respect' is vaguer; the concrete bow is lost.

errors.evidence: and I will bow to you myself.
errors.why: The settling force of 便了 ('and that will settle it') is not conveyed.

items.text: 酒家道：「客官，你須見我門前招旗上面明明寫道：『三碗不過岡』。」
items.answer: The innkeeper said, "Guest, you must see the banner above my door which clearly states: 'Three bowls and one cannot pass the ridge.'"

errors.evidence: you must see the banner above my door
errors.why: 你須見 means 'you surely must have seen'. A present-tense 'must see' reads as an order to go and look, which is the trap named in the key.

errors.evidence: Guest, you must see
errors.why: 'Guest' is a stiff vocative for 客官, where 'sir' or 'customer' would be more natural.

items.text: 戴宗連忙回轉身來問道：「壯士素不曾拜識，如何呼喚賤名？」
items.answer: Dai Zong quickly turned around and asked, "Sir, I have never had the honor of meeting you. How do you address my humble name?"

errors.evidence: How do you address my humble name?
errors.why: 如何 here means 'how is it that / why', but 'How do you address...' reads as 'in what manner' and loses the question about why he knows and calls out the name.

items.text: 見我管待客人在此喫酒，你便與他三五升米便了，何須直來問我！」
items.answer: "Seeing that I am treating guests here with wine, you might as well give him three or five sheng of rice; why must you come straight to ask me!"

items.text: 鲁镇的酒店的格局，是和别处不同的：都是当街一个曲尺形的大柜台，柜里面豫备着热水，可以随时温酒。
items.answer: The layout of the tavern in Lu Town differs from that elsewhere: there is a large counter shaped like a carpenter's square right on the street, and inside the counter hot water is kept ready so that wine can be warmed at any time.

errors.evidence: a large counter shaped like a carpenter's square right on the street
errors.why: 当街 means facing the street, and "right on the street" could suggest the counter sits outdoors; also "the tavern" is singular, whereas 酒店 refers to all taverns in Lu Town.

items.text: 到了年关，掌柜取下粉板说：『孔乙己还欠十九个钱呢！』
items.answer: When the New Year approached, the shopkeeper took down the blackboard and said, "Kong Yiji still owes nineteen qian!"

errors.evidence: When the New Year approached
errors.why: This loses the sense of 年关 as the year-end debt-settling time, though the timing is roughly right.

errors.evidence: took down the blackboard
errors.why: 粉板 is a lime/chalk board for recording debts; 'blackboard' is slightly inaccurate but conveys a similar object.

errors.evidence: nineteen qian
errors.why: The untranslated unit 'qian' is unexplained for an English reader; 'coins' or 'cash' would be clearer.

items.text: 孔乙己便涨红了脸，额上的青筋条条绽出，争辩道：『窃书不能算偸……窃书！……读书人的事，能算偸么？』
items.error: The operation was aborted due to timeout

errors.why: The operation was aborted due to timeout

items.text: 又好笑，又不耐烦，懒懒的答他道：『谁要你教，不是草头底下一个来回的回字么？』
items.answer: She smiled and sighed, answering him lazily, "Who needs your teaching? Isn't it simply a 'hui' with a grass radical on top?"

errors.evidence: She smiled and sighed
errors.why: The narrator is the young waiter ("I"), amused and impatient at once, not a "she" who smiled and sighed; the subject and both feelings are wrong.

errors.evidence: Isn't it simply a 'hui' with a grass radical on top?
errors.why: The 'back and forth' 回 (come-and-go) explanation is lost, so the reader cannot see that 茴 is built from 艹 plus 回.

errors.evidence: Who needs your teaching?
errors.why: The dismissive sense is acceptable, but the candidate uses 'She' with no basis in the first-person narration.

items.text: 我的父亲允许了；我也很高兴，因为我早听到闰土这名字，而且知道他和我仿佛年纪，闰月生的，五行缺土，所以他的父亲叫他闰土。
items.answer: My father gave his consent; I was also very happy, for I had long heard the name Runtu and knew that he was of my own age, born in a leap month, lacking earth among the five elements, so his father named him Runtu.

errors.evidence: he was of my own age
errors.why: 仿佛 means roughly or about the same age, not exactly the same.

items.text: 现在我所谓希望，不也是我自己手制的偶像么？
items.answer: Is the hope I speak of now not also an idol made by my own hands?

items.text: 我看出他话中全是毒，笑中全是刀，他们的牙齿，全是白厉厉的排着，这就是吃人的家伙。
items.answer: I saw that his words were all poison, his laughter held all knives, and their teeth stood in a row of menacingly white—these were the men who eat people.

errors.evidence: a row of menacingly white—these were the men who eat people
errors.why: "a row of menacingly white" is ungrammatical because it is missing a noun such as "teeth" or "fangs".

errors.evidence: these were the men who eat people
errors.why: 家伙 can mean both creature and tool, but the candidate renders it only as "men", losing the dehumanizing and instrument sense; this is a defensible simplification.

items.text: 我也不怕；虽然不吃人，胆子却比他们还壮。
items.answer: I am not afraid; though I do not eat people, my courage is even greater than theirs.

items.text: 子曰：「學而時習之，不亦說乎？有朋自遠方來，不亦樂乎？人不知而不慍，不亦君子乎？」
items.answer: The Master said, "Is it not delightful to study and then review it from time to time? Is it not joyful when friends come from afar? Is it not the mark of a gentleman to be free of resentment when others do not know him?"

errors.evidence: to study and then review it from time to time
errors.why: "From time to time" slightly blurs 時 (at due times, regularly) toward "occasionally", and "review" narrows 習, though the meaning is largely intact.

items.text: 子曰：「巧言令色，鮮矣仁。」
items.answer: The Master said: "He who is glib in his speech and wears an ingratiating expression has little of benevolence."

items.text: 子曰：「君子食無求飽，居無求安，敏於事而愼於言，就有道而正焉：可謂好學也已。」
items.answer: The Master said: "A gentleman does not seek to be well-fed in his eating, nor to be comfortable in his dwelling; he is diligent in his work and cautious in his speech, and seeks out those who are virtuous to correct himself. This may be called true love of learning."

items.text: 子貢曰：「貧而無諂，富而無驕，何如？」子曰：「可也。未若貧而樂，富而好禮者也」。
items.answer: Zi Gong said, "Is it good to be poor without being obsequious and rich without being arrogant?" The Master replied, "That is acceptable. But it is not as good as being poor yet happy and rich yet fond of ritual."

items.text:
牀前明月光，疑是地上霜。
舉頭望明月，低頭思故鄉。
items.answer: Before my bed the bright moon's light gleams, I wonder if it is frost on the ground. I raise my head to gaze at the bright moon; I lower my head and think of my native land.

items.text:
紅豆生南國，春來發幾枝。
願君多采擷，此物最相思。
items.answer: Red beans grow in the southern land; how many branches bloom when spring comes? I wish you would gather them more, for this is the thing that most stirs thoughts of longing.

errors.evidence: how many branches bloom when spring comes
errors.why: 發 means sprout or put forth shoots, not bloom; this is a slight inaccuracy that leaves the meaning intact.

errors.evidence: I wish you would gather them more
errors.why: 'gather them more' is awkward; 'gather plenty' or 'gather many' is the natural English.

items.text:
千山鳥飛絕，萬徑人蹤滅。
孤舟簑笠翁，獨釣寒江雪。
items.answer: Birds fly from the peaks of Qianshan, and footprints vanish from every path. A lone boatman in a straw raincoat and hat casts his line alone into the cold river's snow.

errors.evidence: Birds fly from the peaks of Qianshan
errors.why: 千山 means 'a thousand mountains' (all the mountains), not a place name 'Qianshan'.

errors.evidence: Birds fly from the peaks
errors.why: 鳥飛絕 means birds have ceased flying; the candidate states that birds fly, which loses the stillness and reverses the meaning.

errors.evidence: footprints vanish from every path
errors.why: This is acceptable for the hyperbole, but it is tense-confused and the first line's meaning is already lost.

errors.evidence: A lone boatman
errors.why: The old man (翁) is rendered as 'boatman', so his age is lost.
